    @property
    def context(self) -> Context:

class ICmdLineOption:
    """Base class for command line options."""
    @property
    def names(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the names."""

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the option takes a value."""

    @property
    def help(self) -> str:
        """Get the help: the names, whether a value follows, and the text."""

    @property
    def helpText(self) -> str:
        """Get the help text alone, without the names."""

    @property
    def group(self) -> str:
        """Get the group."""

    @property
    def found(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the option was found."""

    @property
    def matchedName(self) -> str:
        """Get the option name that was matched."""

class CmdLineFlag(ICmdLineOption):
    """Command line flag."""
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '') -> None: ...

class CmdLineOptionI(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '', defaultValue: int | None = None, possibleValues: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> int: ...

class CmdLineOptionF(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '', defaultValue: float | None = None, possibleValues: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> float: ...

class CmdLineOptionD(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '', defaultValue: float | None = None, possibleValues: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> float: ...

class CmdLineOptionBool(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '', defaultValue: bool | None = None, possibleValues: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> bool: ...

class CmdLineOptionString(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '', defaultValue: str | None = None, possibleValues: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> str: ...

class CmdLineListOptionString(ICmdLineOption):
    def __init__(self, names: Sequence[str], help: str, group: str = '') -> None: ...

    @property
    def list(self) -> list[str]: ...

class ICmdLineArg:
    """Base class for command line arguments."""
    pass

class CmdLineArgI(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> int: ...

class CmdLineArgF(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> float: ...

class CmdLineArgD(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> float: ...

class CmdLineArgBool(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> bool: ...

class CmdLineArgString(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hasValue(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> str: ...

class CmdLineListArgString(ICmdLineArg):
    def __init__(self, name: str, help: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def list(self) -> list[str]: ...

class Color1F:

    def __getitem__(self, arg: int, /) -> float: ...

    @property

    @l.setter
    def l(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: Color1F, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: Color1F, /) -> bool: ...

    def __repr__(self) -> str: ...

class ICommand:
    """Base class for commands."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    def exec(self) -> None: ...

    def undo(self) -> None: ...

class CommandStack:
    """Command stack."""
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new command stack."""

    def push(self, command: ICommand) -> None:
        """Execute a command and push it onto the stack."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the stack."""

    def undo(self) -> None:
        """Undo a command."""

    def redo(self) -> None:
        """Redo a command."""

    def observeHasUndo(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observer whether the stack can undo a command."""

    def observeHasRedo(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observer whether the stack can redo a command."""

class Context:
    """
    The systems an application runs on: logging, fonts, I/O, audio and whatever else is added. Everything made from a context is updated by tick().
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new context."""

    def addSystem(self, arg: IBaseSystem, /) -> None:
        """Add a system."""

    @property
    def systems(self) -> list[IBaseSystem]:
        """Get the systems."""

    def getSystemByName(self, arg: str, /) -> IBaseSystem:
        """Get a system by name."""

    def tick(self) -> None:
        """
        Run the systems once: results from other threads are taken in, a player's current frame and time move on, and observers are called. Nothing changes between calls, so a script without an application's event loop calls this in its own loop, for as long as it is waiting for something. It does not wait itself: it takes in only what has finished, so sleep a few milliseconds between calls. A loop of bare calls can run a thousand times before the first frame is decoded.
        """

class DiagFormat:
    """How a sample is turned into the number its format string expects.

    Samples are integers, which is right for counting things and wrong for
    timing them: the resolution wanted for a graph and the unit wanted for
    reading are not the same. Sample in microseconds, divide by a thousand and
    show one decimal, and the graph keeps its detail while the label says
    milliseconds.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def divisor(self) -> float: ...

    @divisor.setter
    def divisor(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def precision(self) -> int:
        """Decimal places. Below zero formats the sample as the integer it is.
        """

    @precision.setter
    def precision(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

def diagText(format: str, diagFormat: DiagFormat, value: int) -> str:
    """Apply a sampler's format to a sample."""

class DiagSystem(ISystem):
    """Diagnostics system."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

    def addSampler(self, id: str, sampler: Callable[[], int], format: DiagFormat = ...) -> None:
        """Add a sampler function. The id is the group and then the name,
        "Group/Name: {0}", the name being the format string for the readout. An
        id already added is left as it is.
        """

    def getFormat(self, id: str) -> DiagFormat:
        """Get how a sampler's value should be formatted."""

    @property
    def groups(self) -> list[str]:
        """The sampler groups, in the order they are shown."""

    @property
    def groupOrder(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        The groups shown first, in order; the rest follow in the order they were added.
        """

    @groupOrder.setter
    def groupOrder(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    def getNames(self, group: str) -> list[str]:
        """Get the sampler names in a group."""

    def hasSampler(self, id: str) -> bool:
        """Get whether the sampler exists."""

    @property
    def samplesMax(self) -> int:
        """Get the maximum number of samples."""

    @samplesMax.setter
    def samplesMax(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def observeSamplesMax(self) -> IObservableSizeT:
        """Observe the maximum number of samples."""

    @property
    def samples(self) -> dict[str, list[int]]:
        """Get the samples."""

    @property
    def tickTime(self) -> datetime.timedelta:
        """Get the system tick time interval."""

    @tickTime.setter
    def tickTime(self, arg: datetime.timedelta, /) -> None: ...

class FileLogSystem(ISystem):
    """File logging system."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, path: str | os.PathLike) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

class FontType(enum.Enum):
    Regular = 0

    Bold = 1

    Mono = 2

    Symbols = 3

def getFontTypeEnums() -> list[FontType]: ...

class FontSystem(ISystem):
    """Font system.

    Add text elide functionality. Add support for gamma correction?
    - https://www.freetype.org/freetype2/docs/text-rendering-general.html
    Use a text-shaping library.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

    @property
    def fonts(self) -> list[str]: ...

    def addFont(self, name: str, fileName: str) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def glyphCacheSize(self) -> int: ...

    def observeGlyphCacheSize(self) -> IObservableSizeT: ...

    @property
    def glyphCachePercentage(self) -> float: ...

    def getMetrics(self, fontInfo: FontInfo) -> FontMetrics:
        """Get font metrics."""

    def getSize(self, text: str, fontInfo: FontInfo, maxLineWidth: int = 0) -> Size2I:
        """Get the size of the given string."""

    def getBoxes(self, text: str, fontInfo: FontInfo, maxLineWidth: int = 0) -> list[Box2I]:
        """Get the character boxes for the given string."""

    def getGlyphs(self, text: str, fontInfo: FontInfo) -> list[Glyph]:
        """Get the glyphs for the given string."""

class ImageType(enum.Enum):
    """Image types."""
    L_U8 = 1

    L_U16 = 2

    L_U32 = 3

    L_F16 = 4

    L_F32 = 5

    LA_U8 = 6

    LA_U16 = 7

    LA_U32 = 8

    LA_F16 = 9

    LA_F32 = 10

    RGB_U8 = 11

    RGB_U10 = 12

    RGB_U16 = 13

    RGB_U32 = 14

    RGB_F16 = 15

    RGB_F32 = 16

    RGBA_U8 = 17

    RGBA_U16 = 18

    RGBA_U32 = 19

    RGBA_F16 = 20

    RGBA_F32 = 21

    YUV_420P_U8 = 22

    YUV_422P_U8 = 23

    YUV_444P_U8 = 24

    YUV_420P_U16 = 25

    YUV_422P_U16 = 26

    YUV_444P_U16 = 27

    YUV_420SP_U8 = 28
    """Semi-planar 4:2:0 8-bit (e.g. hardware-decoded NV12)"""

    YUV_420SP_U16 = 29
    """Semi-planar 4:2:0 16-bit (e.g. hardware-decoded P010)"""

class ImageInfo:
    """Image information."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: Size2I, arg1: ImageType, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: int, arg1: int, arg2: ImageType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def name(self) -> str: ...

    @name.setter
    def name(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def size(self) -> Size2I: ...

    @size.setter
    def size(self, arg: Size2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def type(self) -> ImageType: ...

    @type.setter
    def type(self, arg: ImageType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pixelAspectRatio(self) -> float: ...

    @pixelAspectRatio.setter
    def pixelAspectRatio(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def videoLevels(self) -> VideoLevels: ...

    @videoLevels.setter
    def videoLevels(self, arg: VideoLevels, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def yuvCoefficients(self) -> YUVCoefficients: ...

    @yuvCoefficients.setter
    def yuvCoefficients(self, arg: YUVCoefficients, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def depth(self) -> int:
        """The bits in each sample when fewer than the type holds: 10 or 12-bit
        video kept in 16-bit words with its value in the low bits, as decoders
        hand it over. Zero is the type's own depth. The renderers scale such
        samples up; see getSampleScale().
        """

    @depth.setter
    def depth(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def layout(self) -> ImageLayout: ...

    @layout.setter
    def layout(self, arg: ImageLayout, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def valid(self) -> bool:
        """Is the information valid?"""

    @property
    def aspect(self) -> float:
        """Get the aspect ratio."""

    @property
    def byteCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of bytes used to store an image."""

    def __eq__(self, arg: ImageInfo, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ImageInfo, /) -> bool: ...

class Image:
    """Image."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg: ImageInfo, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: Size2I, arg1: ImageType, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: int, arg1: int, arg2: ImageType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def info(self) -> ImageInfo:
        """Get the image information."""

    @property
    def size(self) -> Size2I:
        """Get the image size."""

    @property
    def width(self) -> int:
        """Get the image width."""

    @property
    def height(self) -> int:
        """Get the image height."""

    @property
    def aspect(self) -> float:
        """Get the aspect ratio."""

    @property
    def type(self) -> ImageType:
        """Get the image type."""

    @property
    def valid(self) -> bool:
        """Is the image valid?"""

    @property
    def tags(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Get the image tags."""

    @tags.setter
    def tags(self, arg: Mapping[str, str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def byteCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of bytes used to store the image data."""

    def zero(self) -> None:
        """Zero the image data."""

    @property
    def data(self) -> memoryview:
        """
        The pixels as a memoryview of (height, width, channels) over the image's own memory, row zero at the top whatever the layout's mirror. Writing to it writes the image.
        """

    def __array__(self, dtype: object | None = None, copy: object | None = None) -> object: ...

class LogItem:
    """Log item."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def time(self) -> datetime.datetime:
        """When the item was logged. Wall clock rather than time since the
        application started: a log is read after the fact, and lining an entry
        up with when something happened is the whole point of it.
        """

    @time.setter
    def time(self, arg: datetime.datetime | datetime.date | datetime.time, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def prefix(self) -> str: ...

    @prefix.setter
    def prefix(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def message(self) -> str: ...

    @message.setter
    def message(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def type(self) -> LogType: ...

    @type.setter
    def type(self, arg: LogType, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: LogItem, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: LogItem, /) -> bool: ...

class IObservableLogItemList:
    """Base class for observable lists."""
    pass

class ObservableLogItemList(IObservableLogItemList):
    """Observable list."""
    def __init__(self, arg: Sequence[LogItem], /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: Sequence[LogItem], /) -> None:
        """Set the list."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: Sequence[LogItem], /) -> bool:
        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: LogItem) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: LogItem) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: LogItem, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Sequence[LogItem], /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    def insertItem(self, index: int, value: LogItem) -> None:
        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[LogItem]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[LogItem]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[LogItem]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> LogItem:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: LogItem, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: LogItem, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

class FrameSeq:
    """Frame sequence."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, range: RangeI64, inc: int = 1) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, min: int, max: int, inc: int = 1) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, frame: int) -> None: ...

    @property
    def range(self) -> RangeI64: ...

    @range.setter
    def range(self, arg: RangeI64, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def inc(self) -> int: ...

    @inc.setter
    def inc(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: FrameSeq, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: FrameSeq, /) -> bool: ...

def toFrameSeq(frames: Sequence[int]) -> list[FrameSeq]:
    """Convert frames to frame sequences."""

def toFrames(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> list[int]:
    """Convert a frame sequence to frames.

    Convert frame sequences to frames.
    """

def addFrame(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq], frame: int) -> list[FrameSeq]:
    """Add a frame to a list of frame sequences, which is kept sorted and
    merged. Frames already in the list are ignored.

    Adding frames in order gives the same result as toFrameSeq(); frames added
    out of order may be split into a different set of sequences that covers the
    same frames.
    """

def getFrameCount(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> int:
    """Get the number of frames in a frame sequence.

    Get the number of frames in a list of frame sequences.
    """

def getRange(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> RangeI64 | None:
    """Get the range."""

def getStep(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> int:
    """Get the step of a list of frame sequences: the smallest spacing between
    its frames, which is one for a sequence of every frame and two for one
    rendered on twos. One for a single frame or none.
    """

def getMissingCount(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> int:
    """Get how many frames are missing from a list of frame sequences: the
    frames at its step, between its first and last, that it does not have.
    Frames 1, 3, 7 and 9 are missing one, frame 5.
    """

def getMissing(seq: Sequence[FrameSeq]) -> list[FrameSeq]:
    """Get the frames missing from a list of frame sequences, as
    getMissingCount() counts them: for frames 1, 3, 7 and 9, frame 5.
    """

class Path:
    """File path.

    Example: file:///tmp/render.0001.exr?user=foo;password=bar
    * protocol: file://
    * dir: /tmp/
    * base: render.
    * number: 0001
    * padding: 4
    * extension: .exr
    * request: ?user=foo;password=bar
    * file name: render.0001.exr
    """
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: str, arg1: str, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: str, arg1: PathOptions, /) -> None: ...

    def get(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def isEmpty(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def hasProtocol(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def hasSeqWildcard(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether this has a sequence wildcard ('#')."""

    @property
    def hasDir(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def hasBase(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def hasNum(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def hasExt(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def hasRequest(self) -> bool: ...

    @property
    def protocol(self) -> str: ...

    @protocol.setter
    def protocol(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def dir(self) -> str: ...

    @dir.setter
    def dir(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def base(self) -> str: ...

    @base.setter
    def base(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def num(self) -> str: ...

    @num.setter
    def num(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pad(self) -> int: ...

    @pad.setter
    def pad(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def ext(self) -> str: ...

    @ext.setter
    def ext(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def request(self) -> str: ...

    @request.setter
    def request(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fileName(self) -> str: ...

    @fileName.setter
    def fileName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    def getFileName(self, dir: bool = False) -> str: ...

    @property
    def frames(self) -> RangeI64 | None:
        """Get the range spanned by the sequence. This is the range from the
        first to the last frame, which for a partial sequence includes frames
        that are missing; use getSeq() for the frames themselves.
        """

    @frames.setter
    def frames(self, arg: RangeI64, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def frameSeq(self) -> list[FrameSeq]:
        """Get the frames in the sequence."""

    @frameSeq.setter
    def frameSeq(self, arg: Sequence[FrameSeq], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seqSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of frames in the sequence."""

    @property
    def isSeq(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether this is a sequence."""

    @property
    def isPartialSeq(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether this sequence is missing frames within its range."""

    def getFrame(self, frame: int, dir: bool = False) -> str:
        """Get a file name with the given frame number."""

    def getFrameRange(self, count: bool = False) -> str:
        """Get the frame range string. When count is true a sequence that is
        missing frames says how many, e.g. "0001-0020 (8 missing)", and one on
        a step with none missing says the step, e.g. "0001-0019 (step 2)" --
        what a file browser shows, so that a broken render is seen before it is
        opened.
        """

    def seq(self, path: Path) -> bool:
        """Get whether a path is part of this sequence."""

    def addSeq(self, path: Path) -> bool:
        """Add a path to this sequence."""

    @property
    def isAbs(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the path is absolute."""

    def testExt(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> bool:
        """Test whether this extension matches one in the given list."""

    def getNumbers() -> str: ...

    def getPathSeparators() -> str: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: Path, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: Path, /) -> bool: ...

class DirListSort(enum.Enum):
    Name = 0

    Extension = 1

    Size = 2

    Time = 3

def getDirListSortEnums() -> list[DirListSort]: ...

class DirListOptions:
    """Directory list options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def sort(self) -> DirListSort: ...

    @sort.setter
    def sort(self, arg: DirListSort, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def sortReverse(self) -> bool: ...

    @sortReverse.setter
    def sortReverse(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def filter(self) -> str:
        """Case-insensitive match against the file name: a substring, or a
        wildcard pattern when it contains "*" or "?". A directory that is
        entered is exempt from the filter -- it is the route to the files, not
        what is being looked for -- while one at the last level is subject to
        it like anything else.
        """

    @filter.setter
    def filter(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def filterFiles(self) -> bool: ...

    @filterFiles.setter
    def filterFiles(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def filterExt(self) -> list[str]: ...

    @filterExt.setter
    def filterExt(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seq(self) -> bool: ...

    @seq.setter
    def seq(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seqExts(self) -> list[str]: ...

    @seqExts.setter
    def seqExts(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seqNegative(self) -> bool: ...

    @seqNegative.setter
    def seqNegative(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seqMaxDigits(self) -> int: ...

    @seqMaxDigits.setter
    def seqMaxDigits(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hidden(self) -> bool: ...

    @hidden.setter
    def hidden(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def depth(self) -> int:
        """How many directory levels to list: 1 is the directory alone. Deeper
        levels follow their directory's entry, each listed with these same
        options, so the order is deterministic. Directory links are listed but
        never entered, which also keeps a cycle of links from listing forever.
        """

    @depth.setter
    def depth(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: DirListOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: DirListOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    """

def expandSeq(path: Path, pathOptions: PathOptions = ...) -> Path:
    """Expand a file sequence. This function will search the directory for
    other frames that match the given file name.
    """

class Random:

    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def getF(self) -> float:
        """Get a random number between zero and one.

        Get a random number between zero and the given value.

        Get a random number between two values.
        """

    @overload
    def getF(self, arg: float, /) -> float:
        """Get a random number between zero and one.

        Get a random number between zero and the given value.

        Get a random number between two values.
        """

    @overload
    def getF(self, min: float, max: float) -> float:
        """Get a random number between zero and one.

        Get a random number between zero and the given value.

        Get a random number between two values.
        """

    @overload
    def getI(self, arg: int, /) -> int:
        """Get a random number between zero and the given value.

        Get a random number between two values.
        """

    @overload
    def getI(self, min: int, max: int) -> int:
        """Get a random number between zero and the given value.

        Get a random number between two values.
        """

    @overload
    def setSeed(self, arg: int, /) -> None:
        """Seed the random value generator.

        Seed the random value generator with the current time.
        """

    @overload
    def setSeed(self) -> None:
        """Seed the random value generator.

        Seed the random value generator with the current time.
        """

class RenderOptions:
    """Render options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def clear(self) -> bool:
        """Clear the canvas before rendering."""

    @clear.setter
    def clear(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def clearColor(self) -> Color4F:
        """Clear color."""

    @clearColor.setter
    def clearColor(self, arg: Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def texturePoolByteCount(self) -> int:
        """Texture pool byte count (enough for two 4K RGBA 16-bit frames). The
        GPU renderer counts an entry with its transfer buffers and holds the
        pool to this at the end of each frame, by the entries that frame did
        not draw with.
        """

    @texturePoolByteCount.setter
    def texturePoolByteCount(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def textureCacheByteCount(self) -> int:
        """Texture cache byte count."""

    @textureCacheByteCount.setter
    def textureCacheByteCount(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def glyphAtlasSize(self) -> int:
        """Glyph texture atlas size. Zero is the renderer's own choice: smaller
        where the graphics API is the more constrained one.
        """

    @glyphAtlasSize.setter
    def glyphAtlasSize(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def log(self) -> bool:
        """Enable logging."""

    @log.setter
    def log(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: RenderOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: RenderOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __truediv__(self, arg: float, /) -> Size3F: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: Size3F, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: Size3F, /) -> bool: ...

    def __repr__(self) -> str: ...

@overload
def aspectRatio(arg: Size2I, /) -> float: ...

@overload
def aspectRatio(arg: Size2F, /) -> float: ...

class ElideMode(enum.Enum):
    """Which end of an elided string to keep."""
    Right = 0
    """Keep the beginning: "ViewLayer.Combi...\""""

    Left = 1
    """Keep the end, for names that differ where they finish, such as a path or
    a layer: "...yer.Combined\"
    """

    Middle = 2
    """Keep both ends: "ViewLa...bined\""""

def elide(value: str, max: int = 32, mode: ElideMode = ElideMode.Right) -> str:
    """Elide a string to at most the given number of characters, not counting
    the ellipsis.
    """

@overload
def getLoremIpsum() -> list[str]:
    """Get filler text."""

@overload
def getLoremIpsum(lineCount: int) -> str:
    """Get filler text."""

@overload
def sleep(arg: datetime.timedelta, /) -> None:
    """Sleep for a given time."""

@overload
def sleep(arg0: datetime.timedelta, arg1: datetime.timedelta, arg2: datetime.timedelta, /) -> None:
    """Sleep up to the given time."""

def toRational(arg: float, /) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Convert a floating point rate to a rational."""

class Timer:
    """Timer."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new timer."""

    @property
    def repeating(self) -> bool:
        """Does the timer repeat?"""

    @repeating.setter
    def repeating(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def start(self, arg0: float, arg1: Callable[[], None], /) -> None:
        """Start the timer."""

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Stop the timer."""

    @property
    def active(self) -> bool:
        """Is the timer active?"""

    @property
    def timeout(self) -> datetime.timedelta:
        """Get the timeout."""

class TextureTypeObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableTextureType, callback: Callable[[TextureType], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableTextureType:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> TextureType:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableTextureType(IObservableTextureType):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: TextureType, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: TextureType, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: TextureType, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> TextureType:
        """Get the value."""

class KeyModifier(enum.Enum):
    """Keyboard modifiers.

    Note: This is a bitfield enum and is not compatible with FTK_ENUM, which
    requires a contiguous Count member. See to_string/from_string below for
    serialization support.
    """
    Shift = 1

    Control = 2

    Alt = 4

    Super = 8

commandKeyModifier: KeyModifier = KeyModifier.Super

    """Get a keyboard modifiers label."""

class MouseClickEvent:
    """Mouse click event."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, arg0: MouseButton, arg1: int, arg2: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def button(self) -> MouseButton: ...

    @button.setter
    def button(self, arg: MouseButton, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def modifiers(self) -> int: ...

    @modifiers.setter
    def modifiers(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pos(self) -> V2I: ...

    @pos.setter
    def pos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def accept(self) -> bool: ...

    @accept.setter
    def accept(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def cancel(self) -> bool:
        """The press was taken away before it was released: a touch gesture
        started, or a finger rested long enough to be the right button
        (longPress). The release ends it without acting on it, so a button
        under the first finger does not click.
        """

    @cancel.setter
    def cancel(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class GestureEvent:
    """Touch gesture event: two fingers dragging and pinching."""
    def __init__(self, arg0: V2I, arg1: V2F, arg2: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pos(self) -> V2I:
        """The point between the fingers."""

    @pos.setter
    def pos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pan(self) -> V2F:
        """How far that point moved since the last event."""

    @pan.setter
    def pan(self, arg: V2F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def zoom(self) -> float:
        """How much the distance between the fingers changed since the last
        event, as a ratio.
        """

    @zoom.setter
    def zoom(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def accept(self) -> bool: ...

    @accept.setter
    def accept(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class IWidget:
    """Base class for widgets."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, objectName: str, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def context(self) -> Context:
        """Get the context."""

    @property
    def objectName(self) -> str: ...

    @objectName.setter
    def objectName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def objectPath(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def backgroundRole(self) -> ColorRole:
        """Get the background role."""

    @backgroundRole.setter
    def backgroundRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def parent(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the parent widget."""

    @parent.setter
    def parent(self, value: IWidget | None) -> None: ...

    def getChildren(self) -> list[IWidget]:
        """Get the children widgets."""

    def moveToFront(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None:
        """Move the child widget to the front of the drawing order."""

    def moveToBack(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None:
        """Move the child widget to the back of the drawing order."""

    @property
    def window(self) -> IWindow:
        """Get the window."""

    def getSizeHint(self) -> Size2I:
        """Get the size hint."""

    @property
    def hStretch(self) -> Stretch:
        """Get the horizontal layout stretch."""

    @hStretch.setter
    def hStretch(self, arg: Stretch, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def vStretch(self) -> Stretch:
        """Get the vertical layout stretch."""

    @vStretch.setter
    def vStretch(self, arg: Stretch, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def setStretch(self, horizontal: Stretch, vertical: Stretch) -> None:
        """Set the horizontal and vertical layout stretch."""

    @overload
    def setStretch(self, arg: Stretch, /) -> None:
        """Set the horizontal and vertical layout stretch."""

    @property
    def hAlign(self) -> HAlign:
        """Get the horizontal layout alignment."""

    @hAlign.setter
    def hAlign(self, arg: HAlign, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def vAlign(self) -> VAlign:
        """Get the vertical layout alignment."""

    @vAlign.setter
    def vAlign(self, arg: VAlign, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlign(self, horizontal: HAlign, vertical: VAlign) -> None:
        """Set the horizontal and vertical layout alignment."""

    def setGeometry(self, arg: Box2I, /) -> None:
        """Set the geometry. If this method is overridden the base method
        should be called.
        """

    @property
    def geometry(self) -> Box2I:
        """Get the geometry."""

    def setPos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None:
        """Set the position."""

    def setSize(self, arg: Size2I, /) -> None:
        """Set the size."""

    def isVisible(self, andParentsVisible: bool = True) -> bool:
        """Is the widget visible?"""

    def setVisible(self, arg: bool, /) -> None:
        """Set whether the widget is visible. If this method is overridden the
        base method should be called.
        """

    def show(self) -> None:
        """Show the widget."""

    def hide(self) -> None:
        """Hide the widget."""

    @property
    def clipped(self) -> bool:
        """Is the widget clipped?"""

    @property
    def clipChildren(self) -> bool:
        """Does the widget clip its children?"""

    @clipChildren.setter
    def clipChildren(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def childrenClipRect(self) -> Box2I:
        """Get the clipping rect applied to the child widgets. By default this
        is the same as the widget geometry.
        """

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Is the widget enabled?"""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def isEnabled(self, andParentsEnabled: bool = True) -> bool:
        """Is the widget enabled?"""

    @property
    def acceptsKeyFocus(self) -> bool:
        """Does this widget accept key focus?"""

    @acceptsKeyFocus.setter
    def acceptsKeyFocus(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def moveToIndex(self, arg0: IWidget, arg1: int, /) -> None:
        """Move the child widget to the given index in the drawing order."""

    @property
    def keyFocus(self) -> bool:
        """Does this widget have key focus?"""

    def takeKeyFocus(self) -> None:
        """Take the key focus."""

    def releaseKeyFocus(self) -> None:
        """Release the key focus."""

    @property
    def tooltip(self) -> str:
        """Get the tooltip."""

    @tooltip.setter
    def tooltip(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    def setContextMenuCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], Menu], /) -> None:
        """Set the context menu callback. The callback is invoked when the
        widget is clicked with the right mouse button, and should return the
        menu to show, or null for no menu. Widgets without a callback pass the
        click to their parent.

        The click is offered to the widgets under the cursor first, so a widget
        that uses the right button for something else keeps it by accepting the
        press; only an unclaimed button opens a menu.

        The menu is created on demand rather than stored so that widgets only
        pay for it when it is used, and so that it can reflect the current
        state, for example disabling paste when the clipboard is empty.
        """

    def childAddEvent(self, event: ChildAddEvent) -> None:
        """Child add event."""

    def childRemoveEvent(self, event: ChildRemoveEvent) -> None:
        """Child remove event."""

    def tickEvent(self, parentsVisible: bool, parentsEnabled: bool, event: TickEvent) -> None:
        """Tick event. If this method is overridden the base method should be
        called.
        """

    def styleEvent(self, event: StyleEvent) -> None:
        """Style event."""

    def sizeHintEvent(self, event: SizeHintEvent) -> None:
        """Size hint event."""

    def clipEvent(self, clipRect: Box2I, clipped: bool) -> None:
        """Clip event. If this method is overridden the base method should be
        called.
        """

    def drawEvent(self, drawRect: Box2I, event: DrawEvent) -> None:
        """Draw event. This runs before the children are drawn, so anything
        drawn here is behind them; use drawOverlayEvent() to draw over them.
        """

    def drawOverlayEvent(self, drawRect: Box2I, event: DrawEvent) -> None:
        """Draw overlay event. This runs after the children are drawn, which is
        where a border or a highlight belongs when the children fill the
        widget.
        """

    def mouseEnterEvent(self, arg: MouseEnterEvent, /) -> None:
        """Mouse enter event."""

    def mouseLeaveEvent(self) -> None:
        """Mouse leave event."""

    def mouseMoveEvent(self, event: MouseMoveEvent) -> None:
        """Mouse move event."""

    def mousePressEvent(self, event: MouseClickEvent) -> None:
        """Mouse press event."""

    def mouseReleaseEvent(self, event: MouseClickEvent) -> None:
        """Mouse release event."""

    def scrollEvent(self, event: ScrollEvent) -> None:
        """Scroll event."""

    def gestureEvent(self, event: GestureEvent) -> None:
        """Touch gesture event. The widget that accepts the first event of a
        gesture receives the rest of it.
        """

    def keyFocusEvent(self, focus: bool) -> None:
        """Key focus event. If this method is overridden the base method should
        be called.
        """

    def keyPressEvent(self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Key press event."""

    def keyReleaseEvent(self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Key release event."""

    def textEvent(self, event: TextEvent) -> None:
        """Text event."""

    def setSizeUpdate(self, value: bool = True) -> None:
        """Set a size update. The sizeHintEvent() and setGeometry() methods
        will be called the next tick of the event loop.
        """

    def setDrawUpdate(self, value: bool = True) -> None:
        """Set a draw update. The drawEvent() method will be called the next
        tick of the event loop.
        """

    def dragEnterEvent(self, event: DragDropEvent) -> None:
        """Drag enter event."""

    def dragLeaveEvent(self, event: DragDropEvent) -> None:
        """Drag leave event."""

    def dragMoveEvent(self, event: DragDropEvent) -> None:
        """Drag move event."""

    def dropEvent(self, event: DragDropEvent) -> None:
        """Drop event."""

class IContainer(IWidget):
    """Base class for widgets that are one child filling them.

    Most composite widgets are a layout, or a scroll area, or a tab widget,
    given the whole of the parent. Written by hand that is the same two methods
    every time:


    Size2I X::getSizeHint() const { return _layout->getSizeHint(); } void
    X::setGeometry(const Box2I& v) {
        IWidget::setGeometry(v);
        _layout->setGeometry(v);
    }


    Deriving from this and calling _setWidget() instead says the same thing
    once. Widgets that lay their children out themselves derive from IWidget as
    before; this is only for the ones that hand everything to one child.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, objectName: str, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def widget(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the child filling this widget."""

class WindowBufferType(enum.Enum):
    U8 = 0

    F16 = 1

    F32 = 2

class WindowBufferTypeObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableWindowBufferType, callback: Callable[[WindowBufferType], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableWindowBufferType:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> WindowBufferType:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableWindowBufferType(IObservableWindowBufferType):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: WindowBufferType, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: WindowBufferType, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: WindowBufferType, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> WindowBufferType:
        """Get the value."""

class IWindow(IWidget):
    """Base class for windows."""
    @property
    def app(self) -> App: ...

    @property
    def windowID(self) -> int: ...

    @property
    def screen(self) -> int: ...

    @property
    def title(self) -> str: ...

    @title.setter
    def title(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def size(self) -> Size2I: ...

    @size.setter
    def size(self, arg: Size2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def minSize(self) -> Size2I: ...

    @minSize.setter
    def minSize(self, arg: Size2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fullScreen(self) -> bool: ...

    @fullScreen.setter
    def fullScreen(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeFullScreen(self) -> IObservableBool: ...

    @property
    def floatOnTop(self) -> bool: ...

    @floatOnTop.setter
    def floatOnTop(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeFloatOnTop(self) -> IObservableBool: ...

    def getWindowInfo(self) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        """Get the window information."""

    @property
    def bufferSize(self) -> Size2I: ...

    @property
    def bufferType(self) -> WindowBufferType: ...

    @bufferType.setter
    def bufferType(self, arg: WindowBufferType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeBufferType(self) -> IObservableWindowBufferType: ...

    @property
    def contentScale(self) -> float: ...

    @property
    def displayScale(self) -> float: ...

    @displayScale.setter
    def displayScale(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeDisplayScale(self) -> IObservableFloat: ...

    @property
    def keyFocus(self) -> IWidget: ...

    @keyFocus.setter
    def keyFocus(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None: ...

    def getNextKeyFocus(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> IWidget: ...

    def getPrevKeyFocus(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> IWidget: ...

    @property
    def tooltipsEnabled(self) -> bool: ...

    @tooltipsEnabled.setter
    def tooltipsEnabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def cursorPos(self) -> V2I: ...

    @property
    def dragDropActive(self) -> bool: ...

    def layout(self, size: Size2I) -> None:
        """Lay the window out at a size, as a resize from the window system
        would.

        Until this happens the window and everything in it has an empty
        geometry, and nothing is under the cursor -- so a test that reads a
        geometry, or aims at one, is reading and aiming at nothing. It does not
        fail; it passes, having checked nothing.
        """

    def click(self, pos: V2I, button: MouseButton = MouseButton.Left, modifiers: int = 0) -> None: ...

    def drag(self, path: Sequence[V2I], modifiers: int = 0, release: bool = True, holdModifiers: int = 0) -> None:
        """Press at the first point, move through the rest, release.

        Moved in steps between the points rather than jumped, because a widget
        that treats a drag as one gesture and a widget that treats every move
        as a separate edit look identical from a single move -- and the
        difference between them is the whole question for undo. Points beyond
        the second are how a drag that goes somewhere and comes back is
        written.
        """

    def setTouchInput(self, value: bool) -> None:
        """Make the mouse events that follow a finger's, or a mouse's again,
        for the widgets that treat a fingertip differently.
        """

    def cancelPress(self) -> None:
        """Let go of what press() holds, cancelled rather than released, the
        way a second finger landing takes a press away.
        """

    def keyPress(self, key: Key, modifiers: int = 0) -> None:
        """Press a key and release it."""

    def text(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Enter text, the way typing does after the key events: letters reach
        a widget as text input, not as key presses.
        """

    def textEditing(self, text: str, cursor: int = 0) -> None:
        """Send an input method composition, the way an IME does while text is
        being composed; committing is text().
        """

    def setIcon(self, arg: Image, /) -> None:
        """Set the window icon.

        Icon images should be of type ImageType::RGBA_U8, with no mirroring,
        memory alignment of one, and LSB memory endian.

        Window icons are not supported on macOS.
        """

    def screenshot(self, arg: Box2I, /) -> Image:
        """Capture a screenshot."""

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the window."""

    def setCloseCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the window close callback."""

    def setFullScreenCallback(self, arg: Callable[[bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set a function called once the window has entered or left full
        screen. On macOS the change animates, and setFullScreen() is only its
        start: what is drawn during the animation is a snapshot of the window
        stretched to the screen.
        """

class IMouseWidget(IWidget):
    """Base class for widgets with simple mouse interactions."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, objectName: str, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

class IPopup(IWidget):
    """Base class for popups."""
    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the popup."""

class DialogSize(enum.Enum):
    Fit = 0

    Text = 1

    Full = 2

def getDialogSizeEnums() -> list[DialogSize]: ...

class IDialog(IPopup):
    """Base class for dialog widgets."""
    def open(self, arg: IWindow, /) -> None:
        """Open the dialog.

        Should setVisible() be used instead of open() and close()?
        """

    def isOpen(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the dialog is open."""

    def setCloseCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the close callback."""

    @property
    def dialogSize(self) -> DialogSize:
        """Get how the dialog is sized."""

    @property
    def textWidth(self) -> int:
        """Get the width of a DialogSize::Text dialog, in characters."""

    def setDialogSize(self, size: DialogSize, textWidth: int = 100) -> None:
        """Set how the dialog is sized, and for DialogSize::Text, how many
        characters wide it is, measured as a label's wrap width is. Fit, the
        default, is what the content's stretch says. Text and Full decide the
        size themselves, whatever the content's stretch, so their content
        should fill the room it is given: labels in it wrapping to fit, a
        scroll widget expanding.
        """

class MenuPopup(enum.Enum):
    """Menu popup type."""
    Menu = 0

    SubMenu = 1

class IMenuPopup(IPopup):
    """Base class for popup menus."""
    @overload
    def open(self, window: IWindow, buttonGeometry: Box2I) -> None:
        """Open the popup.

        Should setVisible() be used instead of open() and close()?

        Open the popup at a position, for example at the cursor for a context
        menu.
        """

    @overload
    def open(self, window: IWindow, pos: V2I) -> None:
        """Open the popup.

        Should setVisible() be used instead of open() and close()?

        Open the popup at a position, for example at the cursor for a context
        menu.
        """

    def isOpen(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the popup is open."""

    def setCloseCallback(self, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
        """Set the close callback."""

    def setPopup(self, type: MenuPopup) -> None:
        """Set the popup type."""

    def setPopupRole(self, role: ColorRole) -> None:
        """Set the popup color role."""

    def setWidget(self, widget: IWidget) -> None:
        """Set the popup widget."""

class IWidgetPopup(IPopup):
    """Base class for popup widgets."""
    def open(self, window: IWindow, buttonGeometry: Box2I, widgetGeometry: Box2I | None = None) -> None:
        """Open the popup.

        Should setVisible() be used instead of open() and close()?
        """

    @property
    def isOpen(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the popup is open."""

    def setCloseCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the close callback."""

    @property
    def widget(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the widget."""

    @widget.setter
    def widget(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def popupRole(self) -> ColorRole:
        """Get the popup color role."""

    @popupRole.setter
    def popupRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

class IButton(IWidget):
    """Base class for buttons."""
    @property
    def checkable(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the button is checkable."""

    @checkable.setter
    def checkable(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def checked(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the button is checked."""

    @checked.setter
    def checked(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        """Get the text."""

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def font(self) -> FontType:
        """Get the font."""

    @font.setter
    def font(self, arg: FontType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def icon(self) -> str:
        """Get the icon."""

    @icon.setter
    def icon(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def checkedIcon(self) -> str:
        """Get the checked icon."""

    @checkedIcon.setter
    def checkedIcon(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def buttonRole(self) -> ColorRole:
        """Get the button color role."""

    @buttonRole.setter
    def buttonRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def checkedRole(self) -> ColorRole:
        """Get the checked color role."""

    @checkedRole.setter
    def checkedRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

    def setHoveredCallback(self, arg: Callable[[bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the hovered callback."""

    def setPressedCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the pressed callback."""

    @property
    def repeatClick(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the button repeats clicks when pressed."""

    @repeatClick.setter
    def repeatClick(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def setClickedCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the clicked callback."""

    def setCheckedCallback(self, arg: Callable[[bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the checked callback."""

def getSettingsPath(directory: str, fileName: str) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Get a settings path."""

class Settings:
    """Settings."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, path: str | os.PathLike, reset: bool = False) -> None:
        """Create new settings."""

    @property
    def path(self) -> pathlib.Path:
        """Get the settings path."""

    def save(self) -> None:
        """Save the settings. The settings are also saved on destruction."""

    def contains(self, key: str) -> bool:
        """Do the settings contain the given value?"""

    def getBool(self, arg: str, /) -> tuple: ...

    def getInt(self, arg: str, /) -> tuple: ...

    def getDouble(self, arg: str, /) -> tuple: ...

    def getString(self, arg: str, /) -> tuple: ...

    def getStringList(self, arg: str, /) -> tuple: ...

    def getJSON(self, arg: str, /) -> tuple: ...

    def setBool(self, key: str, value: bool) -> None: ...

    def setInt(self, key: str, value: int) -> None: ...

    def setDouble(self, key: str, value: float) -> None: ...

    def setString(self, key: str, value: str) -> None: ...

    def setStringList(self, key: str, value: Sequence[str]) -> None: ...

    def setJSON(self, arg0: str, arg1: str, /) -> None: ...

class Window(IWindow):
    """Window."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, app: App, name: str, size: Size2I = ...) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pos(self) -> V2I: ...

    @pos.setter
    def pos(self, arg: V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def maximized(self) -> bool: ...

    @maximized.setter
    def maximized(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def normalGeometry(self) -> Box2I: ...

class ActionCheckType(enum.Enum):
    Check = 1

    Radio = 2

class ActionCheckTypeObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableActionCheckType, callback: Callable[[ActionCheckType], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableActionCheckType:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> ActionCheckType:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableActionCheckType(IObservableActionCheckType):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: ActionCheckType, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: ActionCheckType, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: ActionCheckType, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> ActionCheckType:
        """Get the value."""

class KeyShortcut:
    """Keyboard shortcut."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, key: Key, modifier: KeyModifier) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, key: Key, modifier: KeyModifier, modifier2: KeyModifier) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, key: Key, modifier: KeyModifier, modifier2: KeyModifier, modifier3: KeyModifier) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, key: Key, modifiers: int = 0) -> None: ...

    @property
    def key(self) -> Key: ...

    @key.setter
    def key(self, arg: Key, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def modifiers(self) -> int: ...

    @modifiers.setter
    def modifiers(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

class Action:
    """Action."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, icon: str, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, shortcut: KeyShortcut, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, icon: str, shortcut: KeyShortcut, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, checkedCallback: Callable[[bool], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, icon: str, checkedCallback: Callable[[bool], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, shortcut: KeyShortcut, checkedCallback: Callable[[bool], None]) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, icon: str, shortcut: KeyShortcut, checkedCallback: Callable[[bool], None]) -> None: ...

    @property
    def text(self) -> str: ...

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeText(self) -> IObservableString: ...

    @property
    def icon(self) -> str: ...

    @icon.setter
    def icon(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeIcon(self) -> IObservableString: ...

    @property
    def checkedIcon(self) -> str: ...

    @checkedIcon.setter
    def checkedIcon(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCheckedIcon(self) -> IObservableString: ...

    @property
    def shortcuts(self) -> list[KeyShortcut]: ...

    @shortcuts.setter
    def shortcuts(self, arg: Sequence[KeyShortcut], /) -> None: ...

    def doCallback(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def checkType(self) -> ActionCheckType: ...

    @checkType.setter
    def checkType(self, arg: ActionCheckType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def checkable(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the action carries a checked state at all."""

    @property
    def checked(self) -> bool: ...

    @checked.setter
    def checked(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCheckType(self) -> IObservableActionCheckType: ...

    @property
    def observeChecked(self) -> IObservableBool: ...

    def doCheckedCallback(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool: ...

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeEnabled(self) -> IObservableBool: ...

    @property
    def tooltip(self) -> str: ...

    @tooltip.setter
    def tooltip(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeTooltip(self) -> IObservableString: ...

class ActionGroupType(enum.Enum):
    Click = 0

    Check = 1

    Radio = 2

    Toggle = 3

def getActionGroupTypeEnums() -> list[ActionGroupType]: ...

class ActionGroup:
    """A group of related actions.

    ButtonGroup does this for widgets, and cannot be used for actions: a menu
    makes its own buttons, so the application never sees them, and one action
    commonly drives several -- the same action is a menu item and a tool bar
    button at once. Relatedness belongs where identity is, which is the action
    rather than the widget.

    Radio is the case worth having. Without it an application writes, for every
    set of mutually exclusive actions, an observer that walks the set calling
    setChecked(this one == the current one), and creates the actions with a
    plain callback so that picking one cannot un-pick it. That works and is not
    discoverable from anything.
    """
    def __init__(self, type: ActionGroupType) -> None:
        """Create a new group."""

    @property
    def actions(self) -> list[Action]:
        """Get the actions."""

    def addAction(self, arg: Action, /) -> None:
        """Add an action. The group sets its check type."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Remove every action, leaving them as they are."""

    @property
    def checked(self) -> int: ...

    @checked.setter
    def checked(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def observeChecked(self) -> IObservableInt: ...

    def setCheckedCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int, bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback. The index is which action, the bool its new state;
        for a radio group the bool is always true, since picking one is the
        only thing that can happen.
        """

class ColorControls:

    @property

    @contrast.setter
    def contrast(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def disabledAlpha(self) -> float:
        """Alpha multiplier applied by getColorRole(ColorRole, bool enabled)
        when a widget is disabled. Since widgets are alpha-composited, this
        dims toward the underlying surface.
        """

    @disabledAlpha.setter
    def disabledAlpha(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ColorControls, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ColorControls, /) -> bool: ...

    def getSizeRole(self, role: SizeRole, scale: float) -> int: ...

    def getColorRole(self, role: ColorRole) -> Color4F:
        """Get a color role for a widget state. When enabled is false the
        color's alpha is multiplied by ColorControls::disabledAlpha, dimming it
        toward the surface it is drawn over.
        """

class ObservableMonitorInfoList(IObservableMonitorInfoList):

        """Set the list."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: Sequence[MonitorInfo], /) -> bool:
        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: MonitorInfo) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: MonitorInfo) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: MonitorInfo, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Sequence[MonitorInfo], /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    def insertItem(self, index: int, value: MonitorInfo) -> None:
        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[MonitorInfo]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[MonitorInfo]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[MonitorInfo]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> MonitorInfo:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: MonitorInfo, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: MonitorInfo, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

class AppFiles:
    """Where an application keeps its per-user files: the settings and the log.
    Left empty, no files are kept and the application is responsible for its
    own.

    A suite of applications gives them all the same directory and tells them
    apart by the base name, so that one directory holds the settings and logs
    of all of them rather than one directory apiece.
    """
    def __init__(self, dirName: str = '', baseName: str = '', version: int = 0) -> None: ...

    @property
    def dirName(self) -> str:
        """Directory under the user's documents. Empty keeps no files."""

    @dirName.setter
    def dirName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def baseName(self) -> str:
        """Base name for the settings and log files. Empty uses the application
        name.
        """

    @baseName.setter
    def baseName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def version(self) -> int:
        """Appended to the base name when greater than zero, so that two major
        versions of an application do not read each other's settings.
        """

    @version.setter
    def version(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

class App(IApp):
    """Base class for user interface applications."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, argv: Sequence[str], name: str, summary: str, cmdLineArgs: Sequence[ICmdLineArg] = [], cmdLineOptions: Sequence[ICmdLineOption] = [], appFiles: AppFiles = ...) -> None: ...

    @property
    def settings(self) -> Settings: ...

    @property
    def settingsPath(self) -> pathlib.Path: ...

    @property
    def logFilePath(self) -> pathlib.Path: ...

    @property
    def windows(self) -> list[IWindow]: ...

    @property
    def observeMonitors(self) -> IObservableMonitorInfoList:
        """Observe the monitors."""

    @property
    def fontSystem(self) -> FontSystem: ...

    @property
    def iconSystem(self) -> IconSystem: ...

    @property
    def style(self) -> Style: ...

    @property
    def colorStyle(self) -> ColorStyle: ...

    @colorStyle.setter
    def colorStyle(self, arg: ColorStyle, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def renderer(self) -> Renderer: ...

    @renderer.setter
    def renderer(self, arg: Renderer, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeRenderer(self) -> "ftk::IObservable<ftk::Renderer>": ...

    @property
    def observeColorStyle(self) -> IObservableColorStyle: ...

    @property
    def defaultDisplayScale(self) -> float: ...

    @property
    def autoDisplayScale(self) -> float: ...

    @property
    def displayScale(self) -> float: ...

    @displayScale.setter
    def displayScale(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeDisplayScale(self) -> IObservableFloat: ...

    @property
    def tooltipsEnabled(self) -> bool: ...

    @tooltipsEnabled.setter
    def tooltipsEnabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeTooltipsEnabled(self) -> IObservableBool: ...

    @staticmethod
    def setOffscreenDefault(value: bool) -> None:
        """Set whether applications start offscreen, before any of them exist.

        For test runners and batch tools. An application that is not there to
        be looked at should not be putting windows over whatever the person at
        the keyboard is doing -- and a window that can be clicked while
        something drives it is a run that can be interfered with, which is
        worse than untidy.

        Static because the decision belongs to whoever started the process
        rather than to any one application in it, and a test suite makes
        dozens.
        """

    def writeScreenshot(self, path: str | os.PathLike) -> bool:
        """Write a screenshot of the first window. Returns false when there is
        no window, when the offscreen buffer is not ready, or when the file
        cannot be written; the reason is logged.

        Only useful once the event loop has run: that is what realizes and
        sizes the window and leaves a buffer behind to read.
        """

    def writeWidgetDump(self, path: str | os.PathLike) -> bool:
        """Write the first window's widget tree as JSON; see widgetDump().
        Returns false when there is no window or the file cannot be written;
        the reason is logged. Only useful once the event loop has run and laid
        the window out.
        """

    def exit(self) -> None:
        """Exit the application."""

    def run(self) -> None:
        """Run the application."""

    def tick(self) -> None:
        """Tick the event loop. If this method is overridden the base method
        should be called.
        """

        """Set the number of characters shown when the box is closed, and which
        end of a longer item to keep. Zero, the default, shows the whole of the
        longest item, which is what makes the box as wide as its longest item
        however short the current one is. The menu is never elided, so the
        whole of each item can still be read when choosing.

class ConfirmDialog(IDialog):
    """Confirmation dialog."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, title: str, text: str, confirm: str = 'OK', cancel: str = 'Cancel', parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback."""

class ChoiceDialog(IDialog):
    """Choice dialog: a question answered by one of several buttons, e.g. save,
    discard, or cancel. The last choice is the safe one -- it takes the key
    focus, so the key that takes the dialog at face value is the one that
    changes nothing.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, title: str, text: str, choices: Sequence[str], parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback. It is given the index of the chosen button;
        dismissing the dialog chooses nothing and the callback does not run.
        """

class InputDialog(IDialog):
    """Text input dialog."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, title: str, text: str, value: str, confirm: str = 'OK', cancel: str = 'Cancel', parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[str], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback. It is called once, when the input is accepted with
        the confirm button or the Return key; cancelling closes the dialog
        without calling it.
        """

class ItemButton(IButton):
    """A button that draws the list item states around a widget, for list rows
    built from more than a line of text.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    @property
    def widget(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the widget."""

    @widget.setter
    def widget(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None: ...

    def setFocusCallback(self, arg: Callable[[bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set a callback for when the item gains or loses the key focus."""

    def setDragDropDataCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], IDragDropData], /) -> None:
        """Set the drag and drop data the item offers. Setting it makes the
        item draggable: a press that moves past the drag length starts a drag
        instead of a click.
        """

    def setDragDropCursorCallback(self, arg: Callable[[], Image], /) -> None:
        """Set the image shown under the cursor while the item is dragged."""

class ItemControls(IMouseWidget):
    """A group of controls inside an item row: the mouse stops here, so the
    gaps between the controls go quiet instead of hovering the item underneath,
    and a click that misses a control does nothing rather than acting as a

    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    @property
    def widget(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the widget."""

    @widget.setter
    def widget(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None: ...

class DialogSystem(ISystem):
    """Dialog system."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

    def message(self, title: str, text: str, window: IWindow) -> MessageDialog:
        """Open a message dialog."""

    def choice(self, title: str, text: str, choices: Sequence[str], window: IWindow, callback: Callable[[int], None]) -> ChoiceDialog:
        """Open a choice dialog. The callback is given the index of the chosen
        button; dismissing the dialog chooses nothing.
        """

    def input(self, title: str, text: str, value: str, window: IWindow, callback: Callable[[str], None]) -> InputDialog:
        """Open a text input dialog. The callback is called when the input is
        accepted; cancelling closes the dialog without it.
        """

    def confirm(self, title: str, text: str, window: IWindow, callback: Callable[[bool], None], confirm: str = 'OK', cancel: str = 'Cancel') -> ConfirmDialog:
        """Open a confirmation dialog."""

class Divider(IWidget):
    """Divider widget."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, orientation: Orientation, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

def updateDividers(parent: IWidget) -> None:
    """Show each divider among a widget's children only between visible
    children, and one between any two: a divider beside a group that is hidden
    would stand at the end of the row, or next to another. Call it when the
    children's visibility changes.
    """

class ObservableIDocumentList(IObservableIDocumentList):
    """Observable list."""
    def __init__(self, arg: Sequence[IDocument], /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: Sequence[IDocument], /) -> None:

        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.

class DoubleModel:
    """Double precision floating point value model."""
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    @property
    def value(self) -> float: ...

    @value.setter
    def value(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def setValueSoft(self, arg: float, /) -> None:
        """Set the value, extending a soft range to admit it. This is for
        values the user typed; interactive changes such as dragging use
        setValue(), which always clamps, so they cannot run the range away.
        """

    def observeValue(self) -> IObservableDouble: ...

    @property
    def range(self) -> RangeD: ...

    @range.setter
    def range(self, arg: RangeD, /) -> None: ...

    def observeRange(self) -> IObservableRangeD: ...

    @property
    def rangeSoft(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the range is soft. A value given to setValueSoft()
        beyond a soft range extends the range instead of being clamped.
        """

    @rangeSoft.setter
    def rangeSoft(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def step(self) -> float:
        """Increment the value by a step."""

    @step.setter
    def step(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def largeStep(self) -> float:
        """Increment the value by a large step."""

    @largeStep.setter
    def largeStep(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def stepInc(self) -> None: ...

    def stepDec(self) -> None:
        """Decrement the value by a step."""

    def largeStepInc(self) -> None: ...

    def largeStepDec(self) -> None:
        """Decrement the value by a large step."""

    @property
    def hasDefault(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether there is a default value."""

    def observeHasDefault(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether there is a default value."""

    @property
    def defaultValue(self) -> float:
        """Get the default value."""

    @defaultValue.setter
    def defaultValue(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def observeDefault(self) -> IObservableDouble:
        """Observe the default value."""

    def setDefault(self) -> None:
        """Set the default value.

        Set the value to the default value.
        """

    def clearDefault(self) -> None:
        """Clear the default value."""

class FileBrowserOpenOptions:
    """File browser open options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def title(self) -> str: ...

    @title.setter
    def title(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def path(self) -> pathlib.Path:
        """The directory to open at. Empty stays wherever the browser was last
        left.
        """

    @path.setter
    def path(self, arg: str | os.PathLike, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def mode(self) -> FileBrowserMode: ...

    @mode.setter
    def mode(self, arg: FileBrowserMode, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fileName(self) -> str:
        """A suggested file name for saving."""

    @fileName.setter
    def fileName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def extensions(self) -> list[str]:
        """Restrict the listing to these extensions, e.g. { ".djvr" }. Empty
        shows every file.
        """

    @extensions.setter
    def extensions(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def extensionsLabel(self) -> str:
        """Names the group of extensions: the filter group in the native
        dialog, and the entry shown in place of "*.*" in the built-in one.
        """

    @extensionsLabel.setter
    def extensionsLabel(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def multiple(self) -> bool:
        """Allow more than one file to be chosen. Only meaningful when opening;
        there is one file to save to and one directory to pick.
        """

    @multiple.setter
    def multiple(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...
