class FileBrowserSystem(ISystem):
    """File browser system."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

    def open(self, window: IWindow, callback: Callable[[Path], None], options: FileBrowserOpenOptions = ...) -> None:
        """Open the file browser.

        Open the file browser for more than one file. Set
        FileBrowserOpenOptions::multiple for the choosing to allow it; without
        that this reports the one file chosen.
        """

    def openMultiple(self, window: IWindow, callback: Callable[[Sequence[Path]], None], options: FileBrowserOpenOptions = ...) -> None: ...

    @property
    def nativeFileDialog(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the native file dialog is used."""

    @nativeFileDialog.setter
    def nativeFileDialog(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def model(self) -> FileBrowserModel:
        """Get the file browser model."""

    @property
    def recentDirsModel(self) -> RecentFilesModel:
        """Get the recent directories model.

        What the browser's recent list shows. The directory of every choice
        made in the browser is added to it, whatever the choice was for -- a
        LUT's as well as a movie's -- and it is a list of its own, apart from
        an application's recent files, so those choices do not join them. An
        application that opens files some other way, from the command line or
        by drag and drop, adds their directories here itself if the browser is
        to offer them.
        """

    @recentDirsModel.setter
    def recentDirsModel(self, arg: RecentFilesModel, /) -> None: ...

    def __init__(self, context: Context, model: FileBrowserModel, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

        """Create a new widget."""

class FileBrowserView(IWidget):
    """File browser view widget."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, mode: FileBrowserMode, model: FileBrowserModel, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def reload(self) -> None:
        """Reload the directory."""

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[Sequence[Path]], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback. Carries everything selected, so that opening one
        of several chosen files opens the ones chosen.
        """

    def hasPaths(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether a list of files is shown in place of a directory."""

    def getPaths(self) -> list[Path]:
        """Get the list of files shown in place of a directory."""

    def setPaths(self, paths: Sequence[Path]) -> None:
        """Show a list of files in place of the model's directory: recent
        files, say. They are shown in the order given, each with the directory
        it is in, and the search filter matches against the whole path. The
        extensions chosen in the model do not apply. A directory in the list,
        which is a path ending in a separator, is given to the callback like a
        file. The file system is not asked about the files, so their sizes are
        not shown.
        """

    def clearPaths(self) -> None:
        """Go back to showing the model's directory."""

    def setCurrent(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Set the current item, which selects it: for moving into the list
        from a search box, say.
        """

    def setSelectCallback(self, arg: Callable[[Sequence[Path]], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the selection callback. More than one path only when selecting
        more than one is allowed; empty when nothing is selected.
        """

    @property
    def multiple(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether more than one file can be selected."""

    @multiple.setter
    def multiple(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def selection(self) -> list[Path]:
        """Get the selection."""

    @property
    def search(self) -> str:
        """Get the search filter."""

    @search.setter
    def search(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCurrent(self) -> IObservableInt:
        """Observe the current item."""

    def getRect(self, arg: int, /) -> Box2I:
        """Get the rectangle of an item."""

class FileEdit(IContainer):
    """File edit widget."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, mode: FileBrowserMode, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def path(self) -> str:
        """Get the path."""

    @path.setter
    def path(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[Path], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback."""

class FloatModel:
    """Floating point value model."""
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    @property
    def value(self) -> float: ...

    @value.setter
    def value(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def setValueSoft(self, arg: float, /) -> None:
        """Set the value, extending a soft range to admit it. This is for
        values the user typed; interactive changes such as dragging use
        setValue(), which always clamps, so they cannot run the range away.
        """

    def observeValue(self) -> IObservableFloat: ...

    @property
    def range(self) -> RangeF: ...

    @range.setter
    def range(self, arg: RangeF, /) -> None: ...

    def observeRange(self) -> IObservableRangeF: ...

    @property
    def rangeSoft(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the range is soft. A value given to setValueSoft()
        beyond a soft range extends the range instead of being clamped.
        """

    @rangeSoft.setter
    def rangeSoft(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def step(self) -> float:
        """Increment the value by a step."""

    @step.setter
    def step(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def largeStep(self) -> float:
        """Increment the value by a large step."""

    @largeStep.setter
    def largeStep(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def stepInc(self) -> None: ...

    def stepDec(self) -> None:
        """Decrement the value by a step."""

    def largeStepInc(self) -> None: ...

    def largeStepDec(self) -> None:
        """Decrement the value by a large step."""

    @property
    def hasDefault(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether there is a default value."""

    def observeHasDefault(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether there is a default value."""

    @property
    def defaultValue(self) -> float:
        """Get the default value."""

    @defaultValue.setter
    def defaultValue(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def observeDefault(self) -> IObservableFloat:
        """Observe the default value."""

    def setDefault(self) -> None:
        """Set the default value.

        Set the value to the default value.
        """

    def clearDefault(self) -> None:
        """Clear the default value."""

class FlowLayout(IWidget):
    """Flow layout.

    Children are placed left to right and wrap onto a new line when the next
    one will not fit. Use this where a horizontal layout would be right if only
    it always had the room -- a legend, a row of tags, a toolbar in a panel the
    user can make narrow.

    The height depends on the width, which the size hint has no way to ask
    about, so the layout reports the tallest single child until it has been
    given a geometry, then reports what that width actually needed. Laying one
    out therefore settles over two passes rather than one.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new layout."""

    @property
    def marginRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the margin role."""

    @marginRole.setter
    def marginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def spacingRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the spacing role."""

    @spacingRole.setter
    def spacingRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

class FormGroup:
    """A group of form layouts whose labels share one column width, so that
    forms in separate sections of a panel line up as one would.

    The width is that of the widest visible label in any of the forms, and is
    known when the first of them is sized: a form asks the group, which
    measures the labels of all of them. A form whose section is closed still
    counts, so opening a section does not move the others.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Create a new group."""

def setFormGroup(widget: IWidget, group: FormGroup | None) -> None:
    """Put every form layout among a widget and its descendants into a group:
    for a panel assembled from widgets that each hold a form of their own.
    Forms added to them afterwards are not included.
    """

class FormLayout(IContainer):
    """Form layout."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new layout."""

    def addRow(self, text: str, widget: IWidget) -> int:
        """Add a row."""

    @overload
    def removeRow(self, arg: int, /) -> None:
        """Remove a row."""

    @overload
    def removeRow(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None:
        """Remove a row."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear all of the rows."""

    @overload
    def setRowVisible(self, arg0: int, arg1: bool, /) -> None:
        """Set row visibility."""

    @overload
    def setRowVisible(self, arg0: IWidget, arg1: bool, /) -> None:
        """Set row visibility."""

    @property
    def marginRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the margin role."""

    @marginRole.setter
    def marginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def spacingRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the spacing role."""

    @spacingRole.setter
    def spacingRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def addSpacer(self) -> int:
        """Add a spacer."""

    @overload
    def addSpacer(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> int:
        """Add a spacer."""

    @property
    def group(self) -> FormGroup:
        """Get the group the layout's labels share their width with."""

    @group.setter
    def group(self, value: FormGroup | None) -> None: ...

class GraphLabel:

    @colorRole.setter
    def colorRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property

    @format.setter
    def format(self, arg: DiagFormat, /) -> None: ...

    """Graph widget."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, title: str, labels: Sequence[GraphLabel], parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def setSamples(self, arg0: ColorRole, arg1: Sequence[int], /) -> None:

class GridLayout(IWidget):
    """Grid layout."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new layout."""

    def getGridPos(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Get the grid position of the given child."""

    def getGridRow(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> int:
        """Get the grid row of the given child."""

    def getGridColumn(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> int:
        """Get the grid column of the given child."""

    def setGridPos(self, child: IWidget, row: int, column: int) -> None:
        """Set a child position within the grid."""

    @property
    def rowBackgroundRole(self) -> ColorRole:
        """Get the odd rows background role.

        Get the background role of one row.
        """

    @rowBackgroundRole.setter
    def rowBackgroundRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

    def getRowBackgroundRole(self, row: int) -> ColorRole:
        """Get the odd rows background role.

        Get the background role of one row.
        """

    def setRowBackgroundRole(self, row: int, role: ColorRole) -> None:
        """Get the odd rows background role.

        Set a background role for one row, drawn across the width of the
        layout, margins included, in place of the alternating background: for a
        row that is a heading over the rows below it. None, the default, leaves
        the row as the others are.
        """

    @property
    def marginRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the margin role."""

    @marginRole.setter
    def marginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def spacingRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the spacing role."""

    @spacingRole.setter
    def spacingRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    def setSpacingRole(self, arg0: SizeRole, arg1: SizeRole, /) -> None:
        """Set the spacing role.

        Set the spacing role for each direction. The horizontal spacing is
        between columns and the vertical spacing is between rows.
        """

    def clear(self) -> None: ...

class Label(IWidget):
    """Text label."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, text: str, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        """Get the text."""

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def textRole(self) -> ColorRole:
        """Get the text color role."""

    @textRole.setter
    def textRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def marginRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the margin role. If the horizontal and vertical margin roles are
        different the horizontal role is returned.
        """

    @marginRole.setter
    def marginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hMarginRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the horizontal margin role."""

    @hMarginRole.setter
    def hMarginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def vMarginRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the vertical margin role."""

    @vMarginRole.setter
    def vMarginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    def setMarginRole(self, arg0: SizeRole, arg1: SizeRole, /) -> None:
        """Set the margin role.

        Set the margin roles.
        """

    @property
    def font(self) -> FontType:
        """Get the font."""

    @font.setter
    def font(self, arg: FontType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fontSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the font size."""

    @fontSize.setter
    def fontSize(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def textAlign(self) -> HAlign:
        """Get the alignment of the text within the label."""

    @textAlign.setter
    def textAlign(self, arg: HAlign, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def wrap(self) -> int:
        """Get the width the text is wrapped to, in characters."""

    @wrap.setter
    def wrap(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def wrapToFit(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the text is wrapped to the width the label is given."""

    @wrapToFit.setter
    def wrapToFit(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def elide(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the text is elided to fit the width."""

    @property
    def elideMode(self) -> ElideMode:
        """Get which end of elided text is kept."""

    def setElide(self, elide: bool, mode: ElideMode = ElideMode.Right) -> None:
        """Set whether the text is elided to fit the width the label is given,
        and which end of it to keep. The size hint is then only as wide as the
        ellipsis, so a long text does not widen whatever holds the label; give
        the label an expanding stretch for it to use the room there is. Turning
        it on sets the horizontal alignment to fill, since a left aligned
        widget is laid out at its size hint, and turning it off sets it back to
        left. The text is measured in its font rather than counted in
        characters, and a character is never split.
        """

        """Get whether the selection is valid."""

        """Get the minimum."""

    def max(self) -> int:

    def __ne__(self, arg: LineEditSelection, /) -> bool: ...

class LineEditSelectionObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableLineEditSelection, callback: Callable[[LineEditSelection], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableLineEditSelection:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> LineEditSelection:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableLineEditSelection(IObservableLineEditSelection):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: LineEditSelection, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: LineEditSelection, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: LineEditSelection, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> LineEditSelection:
        """Get the value."""

class LineEdit(IWidget):
    """Text line edit.

    Double click to select text.
    """
    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, model: LineEditModel, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    def getModel(self) -> LineEditModel:
        """Get the model."""

    @property
    def text(self) -> str: ...

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    def clearText(self) -> None: ...

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[str], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback. The callback is triggered when the enter key is
        clicked and optionally when key focus is lost.
        """

    @property
    def hasCallbackOnFocusLost(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the callback is triggered when focus is lost."""

    def setCallbackOnFocusLost(self, arg: bool, /) -> None:
        """Set whether the callback is triggered when focus is lost."""

    def setTextChangedCallback(self, arg: Callable[[str], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the text changed callback. This callback is triggered whenever
        the text is changed.
        """

    @property
    def format(self) -> str:
        """Get the formatting text."""

    @format.setter
    def format(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    def setFocusCallback(self, arg: Callable[[bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the focus callback."""

    @property
    def readOnly(self) -> bool: ...

    @readOnly.setter
    def readOnly(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def selectAllOnFocus(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether all of the text is selected when key focus is gained."""

    @selectAllOnFocus.setter
    def selectAllOnFocus(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def preedit(self) -> str:
        """Get the in-progress input method composition. Empty except while
        text is being composed.
        """

    def selectAll(self) -> None: ...

    def clearSelection(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def font(self) -> FontType: ...

    @font.setter
    def font(self, arg: FontType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def borderRole(self) -> ColorRole: ...

    @borderRole.setter
    def borderRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def rightInset(self) -> int:
        """Get the room kept clear at the right of the text."""

    @rightInset.setter
    def rightInset(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    North = 1

    NorthEast = 2

    East = 3

    SouthEast = 4

    South = 5

    SouthWest = 6

    West = 7

    NorthWest = 8

class Menu(IMenuPopup):
    """Menu."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    def getActions(self) -> list[Action]:
        """Get the actions."""

    def setCurrentCallback(self, callback: Callable[[Action], None]) -> None:
        """Set a callback for the item the user is on: the item under the
        cursor -- a disabled item included, the way a tooltip would show for it
        -- or the current item when navigating by keyboard, announced when the
        menu opens too. It fires with nothing when the menu closes, and it
        reaches into the sub menus.
        """

    def setNeighborCallback(self, callback: Callable[[int], None]) -> None:
        """Set a callback for moving to the menu beside this one, -1 for the
        one on the left and 1 for the one on the right, when the left and right
        arrow keys have nothing to do in the menu itself. A menu bar sets it on
        its menus; a sub menu passes the move to the menu it belongs to.
        """

    def addAction(self, action: Action) -> None:
        """Add an action to the menu."""

    def setChecked(self, action: Action, checked: bool) -> None:
        """Set whether a menu item is checked.

        Remove this function and replace it with an observer.
        """

    @overload
    def setEnabled(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
        """Set whether a menu item is enabled.

        Remove this function and replace it with an observer.
        """

    @overload
    def setEnabled(self, action: Action, enabled: bool) -> None:
        """Set whether a menu item is enabled.

        Remove this function and replace it with an observer.
        """

    def getSubMenus(self) -> list[Menu]:
        """Get the sub menus."""

    def addSubMenu(self, text: str) -> Menu:
        """Add a sub menu."""

    def setSubMenuEnabled(self, menu: Menu, enabled: bool) -> None:
        """Set whether a sub menu is enabled."""

    def addDivider(self) -> None:
        """Add a divider."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the menu."""

    def shortcut(self, key: Key, modifiers: int) -> bool:
        """Handle keyboard shortcuts."""

class MenuBar(IContainer):
    """Menu bar."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    def setCurrentCallback(self, callback: Callable[[Action], None]) -> None:
        """Set a callback for the highlighted item's action, across every menu
        on the bar and their sub menus. It fires with the action when the
        highlight moves, and with nothing when it leaves.
        """

    @overload
    def addMenu(self, text: str) -> Menu:
        """Add a menu."""

    @overload
    def addMenu(self, text: str, menu: Menu) -> None:
        """Add a menu."""

    def getMenu(self, text: str) -> Menu:
        """Get a menu."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the menus."""

    def shortcut(self, key: Key, modifiers: int) -> bool:
        """Handle keyboard shortcuts."""

class IObservablePathList:
    """Base class for observable lists."""
    pass

class ObservablePathList(IObservablePathList):
    """Observable list."""
    def __init__(self, arg: Sequence[Path], /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: Sequence[Path], /) -> None:
        """Set the list."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: Sequence[Path], /) -> bool:
        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: Path) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: Path) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Path, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Sequence[Path], /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    def insertItem(self, index: int, value: Path) -> None:
        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[Path]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[Path]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[Path]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> Path:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: Path, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: Path, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

class RecentFilesModel:
    """Recent files model."""

        """Get the maximum number of recent files."""

    @property
    def observeRecentMax(self) -> IObservableSizeT:
        """Observe the maximum number of recent files."""

    @property
    def recent(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the list of recent files.

        Paths rather than file names: a sequence's range is the path's own and
        is what says whether the entry was one frame or the sequence it sits
        in, so opening it again opens what it opened before.
        """

    @recent.setter
    def recent(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeRecent(self) -> IObservablePathList:
        """Observe the list of recent files."""

    def addRecent(self, arg: Path, /) -> None:
        """Add a recent file."""

    def removeRecent(self, arg: Path, /) -> None:
        """Remove a recent file: one that turned out not to open, say."""

class ItemButtonList(VerticalLayout):
    """A list of item buttons with one focus and one current item.

    The list is the focus unit, the file browser's model applied to rows that
    are widgets: the rows do not take the key focus themselves, the arrows move
    the current item, Return activates it, and Delete removes it. The current
    item outlives the focus leaving the list, so a control that acts on it
    always has a target. A double click on a row is reported on its own, for
    the second thing a row can do.

    The rows are the ItemButton children, in order; other children -- dividers,
    an empty-list label -- are ignored. The caller adds and removes children
    the way it would with a layout, and sets the current item again after
    rebuilding them.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    @property
    def current(self) -> int:
        """Get the current item, or -1."""

    @current.setter
    def current(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def setCurrentCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback for the current item changing from inside the list
        -- the arrow keys browsing it.
        """

    def setActivateCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback for Return on the current item."""

    def setDeleteCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback for Delete on the current item."""

    def setDoubleClickCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback for a double click on a row.

        Counted from the presses rather than the clicks: a callback is free to
        rebuild the rows, and the release of a row that no longer exists never
        arrives.
        """

def setScreenshotTag(widget: IWidget, id: str) -> None:
    """
    Tag a widget so a documentation screenshot tool can find it and emit its bounding box.
    """

    """
    Returns true if the widget carries a screenshot tag (including an empty one).
    """

def getScreenshotTag(widget: IWidget) -> str:
    """Get a widget's screenshot tag, or an empty string if it has none."""

        """

        """Set the callback for the escape key when there is nothing to search
        for: to close whatever the search box is in, say. With text in the box
        the escape key clears it; without this callback and without text, it
        lets go of the key focus.
        """

class Splitter(IWidget):
    """Splitter widget."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, orientation: Orientation, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def setWidgets(self, arg: Sequence[IWidget], /) -> None:
        """Set the widgets, replacing whatever is there.

        Building a tree of splitters by parenting each child one at a time
        means taking the old one apart in the right order first, since a parent
        owns its children: an old splitter whose only other reference is
        dropped stays in the tree and goes on drawing. This does the whole
        thing at once and detaches what it replaces.
        """

    @property
    def split(self) -> float:
        """Get the split value."""

    @split.setter
    def split(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def setSplitCallback(self, arg: Callable[[float], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback for the split being dragged.

        What a linked arrangement is built out of -- a four-up whose rows
        divide together needs each splitter to hear about the other.
        """

    @property
    def border(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the splitter has a border."""

    @border.setter
    def border(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class Splitter2D(IWidget):
    """A splitter that divides both ways at once, into four.

    Two splitters ganged together can hold four widgets, but they are still two
    splitters: the rows divide independently unless something keeps them in
    step, and the point where the divisions cross belongs to neither of them.
    Here there is one division each way and one place they cross, and dragging
    that crossing moves both -- which is the thing a four-up wants and the
    thing two splitters cannot offer.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    def setWidgets(self, widgets: Sequence[IWidget]) -> None:
        """Set the widgets, replacing whatever is there.

        In reading order: top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right. Fewer
        than four fills as many quadrants as there are and leaves the rest
        empty; the divisions do not move to suit.
        """

    @property
    def split(self) -> V2F:
        """Get where the divisions are, each from zero to one."""

    @split.setter
    def split(self, arg: V2F, /) -> None: ...

    def setSplitCallback(self, arg: Callable[[V2F], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback for a division being dragged."""

    @property
    def border(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the divisions have a border."""

    @border.setter
    def border(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class SysLogModel:
    """System log model.

    The system log model keeps a buffer of log items for display in the UI.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    def observeMessages(self) -> IObservableLogItemList:
        """Observe messages (warnings and errors).

        The items are unformatted: a status bar wants the message alone, while
        a list of what has happened wants the time with it, so the choice
        belongs to whoever is showing them. See getLabel().
        """

    def clearMessages(self) -> None:
        """Clear the messages."""

    def observeLog(self) -> IObservableStringList:
        """Observe the log."""

    def clearLog(self) -> None:
        """Clear the log."""

class TabBar(IContainer):
    """Tab bar widget.

    Add scrolling for the tab buttons.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    @property
    def tabs(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the tabs."""

    @tabs.setter
    def tabs(self, arg0: Sequence[str], arg1: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    def addTab(self, arg0: str, arg1: str, /) -> None:
        """Add a tab."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the tabs."""

    @property
    def current(self) -> int:
        """Get the current tab."""

    @current.setter
    def current(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the current tab callback."""

    def setText(self, index: int, text: str) -> None:
        """Set the tab text."""

    def setTabTooltip(self, index: int, tooltip: str) -> None:
        """Set the tab tooltip."""

    @property
    def closable(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the tabs are closable."""

    @closable.setter
    def closable(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def setTabCloseCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the tab close callback."""

    @property
    def scrollBarVisible(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the scroll bar is visible."""

    @scrollBarVisible.setter
    def scrollBarVisible(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

class TabWidget(IContainer):
    """Tab widget."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    @property
    def tabs(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the tabs."""

    def addTab(self, name: str, widget: IWidget, tooltip: str = '') -> None:
        """Add a tab."""

    @overload
    def removeTab(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove a tab."""

    @overload
    def removeTab(self, widget: IWidget) -> None:
        """Remove a tab."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the tabs."""

    @property
    def current(self) -> int:
        """Get the current tab."""

    @current.setter
    def current(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the current tab callback."""

    @property
    def currentWidget(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the current widget."""

    @currentWidget.setter
    def currentWidget(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None: ...

    def setWidgetCallback(self, arg: Callable[[IWidget], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the current widget callback."""

    @overload
    def setTabText(self, arg0: int, arg1: str, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def setTabText(self, arg0: IWidget, arg1: str, /) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def setTabTooltip(self, arg0: int, arg1: str, /) -> None:
        """Set the tab tooltip."""

    @overload
    def setTabTooltip(self, arg0: IWidget, arg1: str, /) -> None:
        """Set the tab tooltip."""

    @property
    def closable(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the tabs are closable."""

    @closable.setter
    def closable(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def setCloseCallback(self, arg: Callable[[int], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the tab close callback."""

class TableCell:
    """Table cell."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, text: str, editable: bool = False, colorRole: ColorRole = ColorRole._None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def text(self) -> str: ...

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def editable(self) -> bool:
        """An editable cell highlights under the mouse, can be made current,
        and calls the table's callback when it is clicked.
        """

    @editable.setter
    def editable(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def colorRole(self) -> ColorRole:
        """Background color role, drawn as a tint."""

    @colorRole.setter
    def colorRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: TableCell, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: TableCell, /) -> bool: ...

class TableRow:
    """Table row."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, cells: Sequence[TableCell], heading: bool = False) -> None: ...

    @property
    def cells(self) -> list[TableCell]: ...

    @cells.setter
    def cells(self, arg: Sequence[TableCell], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def heading(self) -> bool:
        """A heading row is drawn in bold with space above it, and over a band
        the width of the table, with a line beneath it, or both.
        """

    @heading.setter
    def heading(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def visible(self) -> bool: ...

    @visible.setter
    def visible(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: TableRow, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: TableRow, /) -> bool: ...

class TableIndex:
    """Table index."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, row: int, column: int) -> None: ...

    @property
    def row(self) -> int: ...

    @row.setter
    def row(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def column(self) -> int: ...

    @column.setter
    def column(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def isValid(self) -> bool: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: TableIndex, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: TableIndex, /) -> bool: ...

class TableWidget(IMouseWidget):
    """Table widget.

    The table draws its cells as text. To edit a cell, give the table an editor
    widget from the callback: it is placed over the cell until it is closed or
    the key focus leaves it.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None:
        """Create a new widget."""

    @property
    def rows(self) -> list[TableRow]:
        """Get the rows."""

    @rows.setter
    def rows(self, arg: Sequence[TableRow], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def columnCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of columns."""

    def getColumnStretch(self, column: int) -> bool:
        """Get whether a column takes a share of the spare width."""

    def setColumnStretch(self, column: int, stretch: bool) -> None:
        """Set whether a column takes a share of the spare width. Columns are
        otherwise as wide as their widest cell.
        """

    @property
    def current(self) -> TableIndex:
        """Get the current cell."""

    @current.setter
    def current(self, arg: TableIndex, /) -> None: ...

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[TableIndex], None], /) -> None:
        """Set the callback for when an editable cell is clicked, or the return
        key is pressed on the current cell.
        """

    def getCellRect(self, index: TableIndex) -> Box2I:
        """Get a cell rectangle."""

    @property
    def editor(self) -> IWidget:
        """Get the editor widget."""

    @property
    def editorIndex(self) -> TableIndex:
        """Get the cell that is being edited."""

    def openEditor(self, index: TableIndex, widget: IWidget) -> None:
        """Open an editor widget over a cell. The editor should take the key
        focus; it is closed when the key focus leaves it, or when it leaves a
        press of the return or escape key unaccepted.
        """

    def closeEditor(self) -> None:
        """Close the editor widget. The editor is removed on the next tick, so
        this can be called from the editor's own callbacks.
        """

    @property
    def marginRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the margin role."""

    @marginRole.setter
    def marginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def columnLines(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether lines are drawn between the columns."""

    @columnLines.setter
    def columnLines(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def rowLines(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether lines are drawn between the rows."""

    @rowLines.setter
    def rowLines(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def headingLine(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether a line is drawn beneath the heading rows."""

    @headingLine.setter
    def headingLine(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def headingRole(self) -> ColorRole:
        """Get the color role of the heading rows."""

    @headingRole.setter
    def headingRole(self, arg: ColorRole, /) -> None: ...

class TextEditPos:
    """Text edit position."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, line: int, chr: int) -> None: ...

    @property
    def line(self) -> int: ...

    @line.setter
    def line(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def chr(self) -> int: ...

    @chr.setter
    def chr(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def isValid(self) -> bool: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: TextEditPos, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: TextEditPos, /) -> bool: ...

    def __lt__(self, arg: TextEditPos, /) -> bool: ...

    def __gt__(self, arg: TextEditPos, /) -> bool: ...

class TextEditSelection:
    """Text edit selection."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, pos: TextEditPos) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, first: TextEditPos, second: TextEditPos) -> None: ...

    @property
    def first(self) -> TextEditPos: ...

    @first.setter
    def first(self, arg: TextEditPos, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def second(self) -> TextEditPos: ...

    @second.setter
    def second(self, arg: TextEditPos, /) -> None: ...

    def isValid(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the selection is valid."""

    def min(self) -> TextEditPos:
        """Get the minimum."""

    def max(self) -> TextEditPos:
        """Get the maximum."""

    def __eq__(self, arg: TextEditSelection, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: TextEditSelection, /) -> bool: ...

class TextEditModelOptions:
    """Text edit model options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def tabSpaces(self) -> int: ...

    @tabSpaces.setter
    def tabSpaces(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: TextEditModelOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: TextEditModelOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class TextEditModelOptionsObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableTextEditModelOptions, callback: Callable[[TextEditModelOptions], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableTextEditModelOptions:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> TextEditModelOptions:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableTextEditModelOptions(IObservableTextEditModelOptions):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: TextEditModelOptions, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: TextEditModelOptions, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: TextEditModelOptions, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> TextEditModelOptions:
        """Get the value."""

class TextEditPosObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableTextEditPos, callback: Callable[[TextEditPos], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableTextEditPos:
    """Base class for observable values."""

        """Get the value."""

        """Get the number of observers."""

class TextEditModel:
    """Text edit model.

    Implement undo/redo.
    """
    def __init__(self, context: Context, text: Sequence[str] = []) -> None: ...

    @property
    def text(self) -> list[str]: ...

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    def observeText(self) -> IObservableStringList: ...

    def clearText(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def readOnly(self) -> bool: ...

    @readOnly.setter
    def readOnly(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def observeReadOnly(self) -> IObservableBool: ...

    @property
    def cursor(self) -> TextEditPos: ...

    @cursor.setter
    def cursor(self, arg: TextEditPos, /) -> None: ...

    def observeCursor(self) -> IObservableTextEditPos: ...

    @property
    def selection(self) -> TextEditSelection: ...

    @selection.setter
    def selection(self, arg: TextEditSelection, /) -> None: ...

    def observeSelection(self) -> IObservableTextEditSelection: ...

    def selectAll(self) -> None: ...

    def clearSelection(self) -> None: ...

    def undo(self) -> None: ...

    def observeHasUndo(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether there is a command to undo."""

    def observeHasRedo(self) -> IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether there is a command to redo."""

    def redo(self) -> None: ...

    def cut(self) -> None: ...

    def copy(self) -> None: ...

    def paste(self) -> None: ...

    def input(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Handle text input."""

    def key(self, key: Key, modifiers: int = 0) -> bool:
        """Handle key input."""

    @property
    def options(self) -> TextEditModelOptions: ...

    @options.setter
    def options(self, arg: TextEditModelOptions, /) -> None: ...

    def observeOptions(self) -> IObservableTextEditModelOptions: ...

    def setPageRows(self, rows: int) -> None:
        """Set the number of rows in a page."""

class TextEditOptions:
    """Text edit options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @cursorBlink.setter

    @property

    @autoScrollTimeout.setter
    def autoScrollTimeout(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: TextEditOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: TextEditOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class TextEditOptionsObserver:

    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableTextEditOptions, callback: Callable[[TextEditOptions], None], action: ObserverAction = ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

    def setAlways(self, arg: TextEditOptions, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

        """Get the value."""

class TextEdit(IWidget):
    """Text edit widget.

    Double-click to select text.
    """
    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, model: TextEditModel, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    def getModel(self) -> TextEditModel:
        """Get the model."""

    def getScrollWidget(self) -> ScrollWidget:
        """Get the scroll widget."""

    @property
    def text(self) -> list[str]: ...

    @text.setter
    def text(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    def clearText(self) -> None: ...

    def setCallback(self, arg: Callable[[Sequence[str]], None], /) -> None: ...

    def setFocusCallback(self, arg: Callable[[bool], None], /) -> None:
        """Set a callback for when the editing widget inside gains or loses the
        key focus.
        """

    @property
    def readOnly(self) -> bool: ...

    @readOnly.setter
    def readOnly(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def selectAll(self) -> None: ...

    def clearSelection(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def options(self) -> TextEditOptions: ...

    @options.setter
    def options(self, arg: TextEditOptions, /) -> None: ...

    def observeOptions(self) -> IObservableTextEditOptions: ...

    @property
    def sizeHintRole(self) -> SizeRole: ...

    @sizeHintRole.setter
    def sizeHintRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def marginRole(self) -> SizeRole: ...

    @marginRole.setter
    def marginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

class ToolBar(IContainer):
    """Tool bar."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, orientation: Orientation = Orientation.Horizontal, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def marginRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the margin role."""

    @marginRole.setter
    def marginRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def spacingRole(self) -> SizeRole:
        """Get the spacing role."""

    @spacingRole.setter
    def spacingRole(self, arg: SizeRole, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def grouped(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the buttons are grouped."""

    @grouped.setter
    def grouped(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def addAction(self, arg: Action, /) -> ToolButton:
        """Add an action."""

    def addWidget(self, arg: IWidget, /) -> None:
        """Add a widget."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the tool bar."""

class ToolButton(IButton):
    """Tool button."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, text: str, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: Context, action: Action, parent: IWidget | None = None) -> None: ...

    @property
    def popupIcon(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the button has a popup icon."""

    @popupIcon.setter
    def popupIcon(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def secondaryText(self) -> str:
        """Get the secondary text."""

    @secondaryText.setter
    def secondaryText(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

class Tooltip(IPopup):
    """Tooltip."""
    def __init__(self, context: Context, text: str, pos: V2I, window: IWidget) -> None:
        """Create a new tooltip."""
